newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan president calls on rebels to lay down arms.
newsitem.headline: Sudan president calls on rebels to lay down arms.

text.p: Sudan's President Omar Hassan al-Bashir called on Thursday for the rebel factions in his country's civil war to join the peace process.
Bashir made his appeal at a conference in Khartoum, attended by the government's Higher Council for Peace, aimed at trying to end the 14-year old civil war in Sudan.

"I would like to take this opportunity and appeal to all our brothers who are still carrying arms, in and outside the country, to listen to the voice of wisdom and retun home," he said. "They should adopt dialogue and reasoning for settling differences instead of the language of violence and war."
Bashir said the council should work to achieve peace as soon as possible to avoid what he said was the disintegration of African communities by tribal conflict and foreign intervention.
"Such a reality makes it imperative for the Sudanese to work to realise a just and lasting peace in our country."
He said peace was gaining momentum in Sudan but blamed "war mongers and enemies of peace" for derailing efforts.

The Sudanese leader said he hoped a political charter signed in April would be developed into a permanent peace accord signed by all parties including former Sudanese army colonel John Garang, leader of the mainstream Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA).
The SPLA has said it does not trust the present government, which is dominated by Islamists intent on extending Islamic law and which describes the war in the south as a jihad (holy war).
The peace charter was first signed with two small former rebel factions and others later came out in support of the government's peace initiative.
The rebels are fighting for greater autonomy for the black African south against the Arab and Islamised north of the country, which dominates the national government.

The charter says the unity of Sudan should be preserved within its recognised borders. It also offers the southerners a referendum "to determine their political aspirations, but only after peace and stability and a reasonable level of development have been established in the south."
Bashir said more attention would be devoted to developing areas under government control in southern Sudan.
